cell polarity is a conserved mechanism that regulates tissue morphogenesis in both invertebrate and vertebrate embryos.
cell polarity is a key determinant of cell migration, tissue intercalation, and lumen formation.

cell polarity is controlled by conserved pathways during morphogenesis of diverse metazoan tissues, but that there are important differences in the control of cell polarity during morphogenesis that are not conserved across species.

the mechanisms of tissue organization in development.
understanding how the dynamic control of cell polarity regulates the morphogenesis of tissues and organs in developing embryos.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cell polarity is an essential feature of tissue morphogenesis, but the mechanisms by which it is controlled are diverse.
cell polarity in tissue formation is a complex and highly dynamic phenomenon, which is regulated in a tissue-specific manner.
the control of cell polarity is a fundamental and conserved process in tissue morphogenesis, but that different cell types use different mechanisms of polarity control.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cell polarity is a fundamental mechanism for tissue morphogenesis.
the control of cell polarity is a fundamental process in tissue morphogenesis and that the Par/aPKC and the planar cell polarity (PCP) pathways are conserved and important in this process.
the developmental control of polarized cell behaviors is a fundamental mechanism of tissue morphogenesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a remarkable conservation of mechanisms of cell polarity control across the metazoo.
the Par/aPKC and planar cell pathways are both required to control tissue morphogenesis.
cell polarity is not a static, fixed property of a cell but rather a dynamic process that is constantly reconfigured in space and time to drive morphogenesis in developing tissues.
